title: Widen the plate gap
hook: Change plate separation and predict electric-field magnitude.
misconception: electric-field magnitude doubles when plate separation doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply E = abs(V)/d to compare electric-field magnitude when plate separation changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With ideal parallel plates at fixed voltage ignoring edge effects, E = abs(V)/d. When plate separation doubles, electric-field magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model E = abs(V)/d; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider ideal parallel plates at fixed voltage ignoring edge effects, with a nonzero initial result. If plate separation triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on electric-field magnitude?
recall.why: Apply E = abs(V)/d under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
